title: The Fraction Picnic
purpose: Child-friendly illustrated analogy fixture for equal parts, equivalent fractions, prediction, plain language, non-color cues, reduced motion, and creative-content provenance.

learner.audience: Children approximately ages 7-9 learning introductory fractions.

objectives.statement: Identify one fourth as one of four equal parts of one whole.
criteria: Denominator is linked to equal parts in a whole

objectives.statement: Recognize that two fourths cover the same area as one half.
criteria: Matches by area rather than color

objectives.statement: Explain numerator and denominator in age-appropriate language.
criteria: Bottom number names equal parts in a whole

claims.statement: One of four equal parts of one whole is one fourth.
Two fourths cover the same area as one half when the wholes are identical.
Mina and Ravi share identical flatbreads at a fraction picnic.

scenes.title: One whole, four equal pieces
scenes.narration: Mina and Ravi cut one identical round flatbread into four equal pieces. One piece is one fourth.
scenes.visualIntent: A friendly flat vector illustration uses four equal geometric sectors with outlines, hatch patterns, and labels.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A round flatbread is divided into four equal outlined pieces; one is labeled one fourth.

scenes.title: What the two numbers tell us
scenes.narration: The bottom number says how many equal pieces make one whole. The top number says how many pieces we count.
scenes.visualIntent: A large 2/4 label connects the 2 to two selected shapes and the 4 to the four-piece whole.
scenes.captionText: Top: pieces counted • Bottom: equal parts in one whole
scenes.accessibilityDescription: Two callouts connect the numerator two to selected pieces and denominator four to all equal pieces.

scenes.title: Do two fourths match one half?
scenes.narration: Before we move the pieces, predict: will two fourths cover the same space as one half?
scenes.visualIntent: Two fourth sectors and one half shape appear side by side with a short, non-timed pause indicator.
scenes.captionText: Predict: does 2/4 cover the same area as 1/2?
scenes.accessibilityDescription: Two fourth-piece shapes and one half-circle are presented for comparison without revealing the answer.

scenes.title: Same area, different names
scenes.narration: Yes. Two equal fourths fit exactly over one half. Two fourths and one half are equivalent fractions.
scenes.visualIntent: Default motion slides the pieces together slowly; reduced motion crossfades between before and exact-overlap states.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: The two fourth pieces exactly cover the same semicircle area as one half.

scenes.title: Show what you know
scenes.narration: Point to one fourth, tell what the bottom four means, and choose the shape equal to two fourths.
scenes.visualIntent: Three untimed practice prompts have large targets, keyboard equivalents, shape labels, and no color-only answer.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: Three plain-language questions are presented one at a time with large labeled choices.

qualityAssertions.description: All fourth pieces have equal computed area and exactly tile the whole.
Two fourth shapes exactly cover the half shape.
Narration defines terminology, uses short sentences, and avoids unexplained algebra.
Every spatial animation has an equivalent static or crossfade state.
Outlines, patterns, text, and shape position convey every distinction without color.

provenance.notes: Named children and picnic scenario are fictional; all visuals must be generated deterministically from shapes, not remote media.
